newsitem.title: DENMARK: POLL - Danish ISS seen back in H1 97 profit.
newsitem.headline: POLL - Danish ISS seen back in H1 97 profit.

text.p: Seven analysts forecast on Friday that Danish cleaning group International Service System (ISS) would swing back into profit in the first-half of 1997.

The panel predicted average interim profits before tax and extraordinary items of 184 million crowns, compared to 1996's first-half loss of 146 million crowns, with estimates ranging from 164-235 million crowns.
ISS incurred vast losses in early 1996 from a falsified accounts scandal in its U.S. ISS Inc unit, which it eventually sold last December to Canada's Aaxis Ltd.
The analysts cited advances in ISS operations in Scandinavia and Europe as reasons for their expectations of a swing back into interim 1997 profit.
ISS FIRST-HALF 1997 FORECAST (seven analysts, turnover in billions of crowns, other data in millions of crowns)
ISS is to release its 1997 interim results on August 19. --Stig Orskov Pedersen, Copenhagen newsroom +45-33969659
